newsitem.title: GERMANY: Couple say 'I do' before Berlin's Brandenburg Gate.
newsitem.headline: Couple say 'I do' before Berlin's Brandenburg Gate.

text.p: A German couple exchanged marriage vows on an open-topped bus in front of the Brandenburg Gate on Monday in what Berlin registry officials hope will start a bizarre trend.
Dagmar Erdmann and Andreas Paetzel marched down the aisle of the coach provided by the Berlin transport authority and took their vows before 38 family and friends.

The Brandenburg Gate became the city's symbol of unity after 1989, when East German leaders opened the Berlin Wall that formed the Cold War divide between the two Germanys and thousands of East Germans streamed over to the West.
Erdmann and Paetzel are the first couple to use the new service, run by the transport authority and city registry office to promote the city as a site for weddings.

Authorities provided a single-decker bus emblazoned with the slogan "get married in Berlin" with a roll-back roof, complete with a refrigerator for champagne and intercom service to play the wedding march, for a fee of 650 marks ($380) for three hours.
Despite steady rain, the wedding party rolled back the canvas top and officials called the day a success.

"You can attract a lot of couples looking for a place for their wedding with this kind of offer," said Sylvia Brenke, registry official for the Berlin district of Tiergarten. "We have even had some inquiries from Japan."
